text:
A Lake Wind Advisory is up, and this is no afternoon for a casual outing on the water. Burlington is already living the forecast, with steady rain, fog, 54 degrees, and the kind of damp chill that gets into everything. The rain continues through the afternoon, with a few heavier bursts and thunderstorms becoming more likely after 5. Expect a high near 59, southeast winds around 16 mph with stronger gusts, and roughly three quarters to an inch of rain by tonight.

The lake will turn rough, with southeast winds building to 15 to 25 knots and waves reaching 4 to 6 feet, so stay off broad water this afternoon and evening. Showers and a few thunderstorms keep going tonight, with another half to three quarters of an inch possible. Wednesday is an improvement, though still gray, breezy, and showery early, with a high near 60. Plan for a wet commute home today, and wait until tomorrow afternoon for easier outdoor plans.

week.blurb: Rain and thunderstorms take over this afternoon and tonight, with nearly two inches possible and no dry window worth planning around.
A damp start fades into a mostly cloudy day, but the high could land anywhere from the upper 50s to mid 60s.
Sunny and cool Thursday, near 54, with rain arriving after dark and likely continuing into Friday.
Friday looks like a raw, rainy day near 56, with stronger winds and rain lingering into the night.
A blustery mix of rain and snow showers keeps Saturday cold near 43, with improving skies after dark.
Sunshine returns Sunday, but a cool breeze keeps the high near 49, a decent day for a shorter outdoor plan.
Monday looks mostly sunny and milder, with a south wind and a high near 57.
